A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. Earlier sections and experiments can be matched reliably to their revised or renumbered counterparts.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original teacher–student experiments, including loss landscapes, training outcomes, constraint relaxation, and spherical-signal experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain these original experiments and their reported outcomes.

M1.justification: The network architectures, equivariance constraints, parameterizations, and procedure of training a constrained network before relaxing its constraints are retained. The new optimizer discussion introduces no implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic teacher–student tasks involving permutation symmetry and spherical signals. The spherical input representations and ReLU/erf experiments are retained from v1 Appendix C in v2 Appendix E.

E2.justification: The constrained-versus-relaxed network comparisons are unchanged. Newly discussed prior methods in v2 Appendix B are not evaluated as additional experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The stated experimental settings remain unchanged, including 100 exact-loss gradient-descent steps at learning rate 0.1 in Section 4.3. Appendix B newly identifies SGD with incompletely augmented batches for relaxation; this is additional disclosure, not an established protocol change.

E4.justification: The initialization sweeps, parameterization comparisons, alternative activation, and spherical-input analyses are retained. Appendix F discusses optimizer implications without adding optimizer experiments or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both versions show the same results across different teacher initialization seeds without aggregate uncertainty estimates or significance tests. The new checklist explains the absence of statistical analysis but adds no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The empirical plots and reported findings are unchanged: v1 Figures 4–13 correspond to v2 Figures 5–14, preserving loss landscapes, final losses, weight visualizations, and relaxation trajectories. The added introductory figure is conceptual.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 gains the previously omitted orthogonality assumption, while its main-text nondegeneracy requirement is narrowed to the hidden-subspace minimum. Theorem 3.4 adds and proves the zero-output elimination case, and Lemma 3.2's proof removes finite-group averaging. Appendix C.1 adds definitions of infinite permutation representations. These substantively revise the formal treatment, although Appendix D retains the stronger nondegeneracy requirement.

C1.justification: The rewritten takeaways emphasize hidden symmetries and constraint enforcement, but the central claims remain: hidden symmetries can induce critical points and spurious minima, and relaxation can sometimes escape through a different hidden-layer representation. The conclusion retains the same contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly discusses when the theorem assumptions hold, including limitations for wide preceding layers. Appendix B explains escape from equivariant subspaces through incompletely augmented SGD batches. Appendix F adds substantive interpretations concerning weight decay, parameter-dependent learning rates, and saddle dynamics.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly discloses SGD and incomplete batch augmentation for the relaxation experiment. The checklist additionally states that code and full experimental details accompany supplemental material. Actual code availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: New Appendix B develops connections to Nordenfors et al.'s equivariant optimization analysis and Arjevani and Field's families of spurious minima. Appendix F adds connections to saddle-to-saddle dynamics. This substantially expands positioning relative to closely related theory rather than merely adding citations.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory takeaways are rewritten, theorem conditions are organized explicitly, and notation, related-work, optimizer-discussion, acknowledgment, and checklist material is added. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain intact; the original appendices are retained and renumbered.

P2.justification: v2 adds a two-panel conceptual Figure 1 and a notation table. Existing figures are retained as Figures 2–14, with limited placement and caption-layout changes; the empirical displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs a missing assumption in Theorem 3.3 and completes Theorem 3.4's previously unfinished zero-output case. Added discussion improves understanding of applicability and SGD-mediated escape. These provide concrete gains in rigor and clarity, although inconsistent nondegeneracy requirements and the still-incomplete boundary-lemma proof limit the improvement.
